class: Each capture route had its own code, so masking added to one never reached the others
symptom: Found in the architecture review of 1 October: the page text was masked (hide_secrets, f015), but the forensic dumper (state_machine), the review package and the hand-over evidence wrote full screenshots and raw page HTML, and one screenshot was sent to the AI to read a page. A typed password shows in a screenshot; raw HTML carries hidden form tokens, CSRF meta values and session data in scripts. No leak was found -- these were open paths.
root_cause: There was no single capture service: seven places called page.screenshot() or page.content() directly, each written for its own purpose, and the masking was added to the one route that had leaked before (the page text). Nothing limited how long evidence was kept.
why_tests_missed: The secrets tests (f015) covered the page text and the forensic accessibility tree only; no test looked inside a saved screenshot's inputs or the saved HTML.
fix: evidence.py: screenshot() paints over every secret box (password, passcode, one-time code, PIN, card number; by type, autocomplete and name) and returns bytes for the AI; html() empties scripts, removes hidden-input and secret-box values and token meta tags; page_text() hides secrets; capture() writes all three; prune() removes screenshots and page copies older than EVIDENCE_KEEP_DAYS (default 30) at each run's start, keeping output/<job>/pages (the replay guard's record) and documents. Every capture point now goes through it: apply_flow (evidence, stop pages, confirmations), state_machine (forensic dump), browser_automation (AI screenshot, account failures, review package), page_agent (account pages), safety (sponsorship mismatch).
prevention: Route every screenshot, page copy and page text through one capture service that sanitizes each format and applies retention; forbid direct page.screenshot()/page.content() writes elsewhere.
